A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable matching of retained, revised, and added material.

before.justification: v2 reports original fingerprint detection, utility, robustness, and stealth experiments in Section 5 and Appendices B, C, and E.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds instruction-tuning robustness, finetuneability, and fingerprint-leakage experiments in Appendices B.4, B.5, and C.5.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the training losses, and concatenated-response detection remain unchanged. The correction to Eq. (3) aligns it with the detector already specified in v2 Appendix D; it does not introduce a new procedure. The added experiments use existing method components.

E1.justification: v3 substantially extends test coverage with Galician finetuning/evaluation, completion-to-chat deployment, Pirate and weather-restricted prompt scenarios, and cross-domain leakage probes using CodeAlpaca and WHO-derived health questions. French, math, medicine, and completion-model coverage already existed in v2.

E2.justification: Instructional Fingerprinting and Scalable Fingerprinting remain the evaluated competing methods, including in the expanded Table 5. The original-model utility controls and full-watermark ablation are retained. The new translator is an attack component, not an added fingerprinting baseline.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include one-epoch instruction tuning with a changed chat template, paired utility measurements before and after French/Galician finetuning, and unregularized math-watermark leakage testing with 1000 queries per domain. Appendix B.2 adds mixed GPT5-MINI/GEMINI2.5-FLASH-LITE back-translation, and C.3 adds FrenchBench accuracy. The existing Appendix A protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether fingerprints survive instruction tuning, hinder subsequent finetuning, or leak outside their target domain. Additional adversarial prompts and mixed-model translation expand robustness testing, while FrenchBench measurements extend the watermark-strength trade-off analysis. The earlier full-watermark and regularization ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions calculate FSR over five independent detection runs and average query-scaling results over five runs; the new plots follow this practice. No new uncertainty-reporting or significance-testing procedure is introduced. Appendix D already contains the variance-corrected statistical test.

E6.justification: Existing table values and plotted results are retained. New results include FSR 1.0 across the added Table 5 attacks, detection after instruction tuning, and no detected leakage in the tested off-domain probes. Table 6 reports FrenchBench scores before/after finetuning of 59/63 for the original model versus 57/59 for the fingerprinted model, and GalicianBench scores of 46/50 versus 46/51. C.3 adds accuracy endpoints of 0.61 and 0.57, although its delta = 5 endpoint conflicts with the stated 0.5–4 sweep.

T1.justification: Eq. (3) moves beta(omega) outside the denominator's square root, correcting its normalization to agree with Eqs. (8) and (10), already present in v2. Theorem D.1, its assumptions, and its proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, listed main contributions, and conclusion retain the same novelty, stealth, and robustness claims. Added usage-tracking motivation and supporting appendix experiments do not redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: v3 softens high entropy from a requirement to a factor affecting query cost. It acknowledges the existing HumanEval decline and hypothesizes a general small-model finetuning cause. New discussion interprets finetuneability and leakage results, acknowledges higher embedding cost, and qualifies the license-enforcement motivation. The final limitations paragraph is unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the statement that code accompanies the submission with a repository link and documents settings and prompts for the added studies. New Table 9 reports embedding costs: approximately 81.92M tokens/$6 for the proposed method, versus 0.71M tokens/under $1 for IF and 7.19M tokens/under $1 for SF. Existing core hyperparameter and hardware disclosures remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds timing-based identification as an alternative, citing Carlini and Nasr, Song et al., and Alhazbi et al., while discussing possible defenses. Other additions support the licensing discussion, small-model finetuning interpretation, and new datasets. Positioning against query-key fingerprinting remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely retained, with localized discussion edits, added appendix subsections, and an ICLR 2026 publication header. Some references to full-watermark robustness incorrectly change from B.3 to B.5, although that experiment remains in B.3.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 5 and 9, Tables 6 and 9, and four rows to Table 5. Existing figure content is retained, with some relocation and renumbering. The visual style remains stable; the first Appendix G example is now split across pages.

improvement.justification: The added instruction-tuning, finetuneability, and leakage tests strengthen practical validation. Correcting Eq. (3) removes an internal inconsistency, while code-access and cost information improve transparency. These benefits yield a limited net improvement: the central evidence is unchanged, the new finetuneability conclusion overstates Table 6's smaller French gains, and C.3 introduces an inconsistent watermark-strength endpoint.
